title: Circulants with circular chromatic index in the upper half
scope: Mazák–Zrubák, arXiv:2603.08822, Section 8: no graph with `Δ>=8` and circular chromatic index in `(Δ+1/2, Δ+1)` was known. For every `g>=2` the circulant `C_{6g+1}(1,...,2g-2, 2g+1, 3g)` is `4g`-regular and `4g`-connected with `χ'_c = 4g+2/3`, and `C_25(1,2,3,7,...,12)` is 18-regular and 18-connected with `χ'_c = 75/4`. This answers the non-trivial reading of their Problem 6 for `d ≡ 0 mod 4`, `d>=8`, and for `d=18`; Problem 7 is not answered. Computer-certified further examples include `C_31(1,2,3,7,...,12)` with `χ'_c = 93/5` and non-regular graphs with `Δ ≡ 1, 2 mod 4`, `25<=Δ<=54`. One independent model referee pass.

title: Erdős–Hajnal–Szemerédi independence-ratio problem
scope: A graph of cardinality at most the continuum is countably colorable if its finite subgraphs have bounded vector chromatic number. Finite graphs can have bounded Hall ratio and arbitrarily large vector chromatic number.
judgment: For a fixed vector-coloring bound K, compactness gives a global Gram representation. On at most continuum many vertices the basis elements admit distinct binary strings. This is a countable-colorability criterion for bounded finite vector chromatic number. A uniform Hall-ratio bound alone is precisely the missing implication.

title: Multicolor Steiner triple system sail problem
scope: For every fixed number of colors, almost every Steiner triple system has a positive density of monochromatic sails in every vertex subset of fixed positive density, simultaneously for all block colorings.
judgment: For a nonexceptional center, each internal block in the selected color-neighbor set produces a distinct sail. Linearity rules out two transversal vertices on a single center block. The nested induced sets therefore control every used color simultaneously. The union bound for dense vertex sets and the triangle-removal transfer are statements about uniformly random hosts, whereas the separate packing assertion assumes a small independence number. The all-host multicolor target stays open.

title: Németh–Seberry–Shu conjecture
scope: The number of distinct permanent values of prime-order binary circulants grows superlinearly, contrary to the 1979 conjecture. A refinement gives a quadratic lower bound.
judgment: Checked the role of the uniformity assumption in Divoux–Wang, Proposition 3.1 and Remark 2.1. The proof first fixes finitely many amplitudes and then takes the prime order large, so no convergence rate is needed for the basic disproof. The translation action gives permanent congruent to the row sum modulo the prime: the fixed permutations are exactly allowed translations. An independent matching-count dynamic program confirmed the congruence for every binary circulant at orders 2, 3, 5 and 7. The quadratic strengthening has its own proof.

The earlier receipt for the theta-kernel file matches the historical receipt commit.

scope: The values below 1/6 are exactly (P−1)/(6P) for P ≥ 7 congruent to ±1 modulo 6. Cordella’s nine sporadic sextuples exhaust the exceptions to the three known families. Lean verifies realization of every proposed value by six distinct positive primitive speeds; actual rational-lattice, Gram and integer-factor components are proved, and the registered norm wrappers use the proved four-speed bound and retain `hplane`. Universal classification remains incomplete. Lean also proves the conditional two-parameter radius estimate; the finite plane enumeration remains incomplete.
judgment: The computational proof has several independent stages. A previous successful GitHub-hosted run used the same result directory and modular-sieve source as the audited tree. Its log confirms four prime-product bounds (145 primes), 15 three-parameter covers, 78 noncritical maps and nine sporadic values. The degree of partial Lean coverage remains as stated on the landing page. [Hosted replay](https://github.com/1337isnot1337/solved-conjectures/actions/runs/45822175370/job/139916962874).

title: Wagner's Laguerre-operator conjecture
scope: Complete proposed disproof of Conjecture 4.3 as stated in arXiv:2108.01827v2. The positive shifted Laguerre–Pólya function exp(z)+1 is sent by the first Laguerre operator to −exp(z), which has negative coefficients at every index. judgment: Earlier exact disproof. The September manuscript uses the very same witness 1 + exp(z). Its approximants c + (1 + az/N)^N meet the shifted-class condition and the Taylor derivatives are eventually positive. L₁(1 + exp z) = −exp z, whose Taylor derivatives are all negative. The earlier proof also handles every odd positive Laguerre index. The archived repository landing page simultaneously claimed no Lean and a complete Lean proof.

scope: The construction and proof establish the required peaks for every prescribed exponent set with at most $K H^\sigma$ points in each interval of length $H\ge1$, for any fixed $\sigma<1$ with $\sigma>0$. title: Erdős–Sauer conjecture
scope: **Theorem.** Fix $r\ge3$. Define $\gamma_3=20/7$ and $\gamma_r=r-1$ for $r\ge4$. Uniformly over $n$-vertex $r$-graphs, ```math D(G)\ \le\ \operatorname{ex}_r(n,K)-(r-\gamma_r)\nu(G)+o(n^r). ``` Consequently the maximum decomposition number is $\operatorname{ex}_r(n,K)+o(n^r)$. Every sequence attaining that value to within $o(n^r)$ is within $o(n^r)$ edge deletions of a $K$-free sequence with $\operatorname{ex}_r(n,K)-o(n^r)$ edges. For any fixed $\epsilon\gt0$, the exact conjectured bound holds for sufficiently large $n$ if $|E(G)|\ge\operatorname{ex}_r(n,K)+\epsilon n^r$.

title: Erdős–Selfridge conjecture
scope: Hough and Nielsen prove that some modulus of every distinct covering system is divisible by 2 or 3. Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe and Tiba prove that the least common multiple is divisible by one of 2, 9 or 15, and their squarefree theorem rules out all-odd distinct systems with squarefree moduli. Dai, Li, Li and Yi strengthen the all-odd condition to divisibility of the least common multiple by 45 and show that some modulus is at most 9. Their least-common-multiple result permits the factors 9 and 5 to come from different moduli.

HIGH-THROUGHPUT FABRICATION AND DEFECT SORTING OF BIOMEDICAL MICRO/NANOROBOTS AT THE LIMIT  High-Throughput Fabrication x Automated Sorting x Defect Identification  This 770-page Research Working Edition develops a falsification-oriented, nonclinical architecture for high-throughput fabrication and defect sorting of biomedical micro/nanorobots. It asks whether production can accelerate while complete material accounting, class-specific defect evidence, rare-hazard detection, rejection burden and independent terminal function remain directly measurable on the entire unselected population. Gross line speed, a visually well-formed unit or selected best specimens are not accepted as qualified capacity.  The monograph contains 30 distinct mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 single-page investigations, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 genuinely distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos. Model families include qualified output rate, Little's law, physical material balance, stagewise joint yield, OEE, Poisson and overdispersed defect counts, beta-binomial clustering, confusion matrices, precision-recall, hazardous-miss bounds, sequential likelihood evidence, cost-sensitive thresholds, reject options, multimodal likelihood and covariance fusion, gauge R&R, drift, conformal anomaly detection, selective risk, queue stability, data reconciliation, capture-recapture prevalence and noncompensable release logic.  The minimum demonstrator uniquely tracks 100,000 units and blindly injects five defect classes, including rare hazardous defects and one clustered carrier-level failure. Multimodal sorting competes with sampling microscopy and single-channel sorting under identical material, live-time, station, compute, retest and labor budgets. Every unit receives an auditable branch and stratified independent terminal verification. Hazardous escape above the frozen ceiling, unexplained material imbalance, forced classification of unsupported evidence, omitted rejects or qualified-capacity gain purchased solely by higher rejection is a hard veto. title: erdos ruzsa prime covers
scope: **Theorem.** Fix $C>0$ and $0<\theta<1/2$, and put $y=N^\theta$. Choose one uniform residue independently for every prime $y<p\le N$. There are constants $a,b>0$, depending only on $C,\theta$, such that with probability at least ```math 1-\exp(-bN^\theta\log N), ``` at least $aN$ integers survive **every** choice of a set $P$ of small primes up to $y$ with $\sum_{p\in P}1/p\le C$ and arbitrary classes modulo these primes, in addition to **all** the larger random classes. The conclusion still holds with $aN/2$ survivors if any subset of large classes is discarded and any remaining large classes of total reciprocal cost at most $a/4$ are reassigned adversarially.

scope: Conjecture 8.1 asks for magic positivity of every generalized parking-function polytope $\mathfrak X_n(\mathbf b)$, $n\ge3$, $b_i\ge1$.
